core_obligations: Assume the source countably indexed, write both spaces as filtered colimits of affine schemes, and for each stage of the source choose a stage of the target through which it factors (proof lines 4555-4562).
For each stage of the target, note that its fibre product with the source is affine and hence factors through some stage of the source, and display the resulting diagram (proof lines 4562-4568).

Show the existence of the dotted arrow in that diagram: choose a stage above both, write the two closed subschemes as ideals of its coordinate ring, observe that the containment holds after extending along the morphism from the source, and descend it using that the relevant fibre product is faithfully flat over the stage (proof lines 4574-4589).
Conclude that the chosen stages of the target form a cofinal countable subsystem of its presentation, so that the target is countably indexed (proof lines 4571-4576).
Give the converse direction by the descent statement for countable indexedness (proof lines 4591-4593).
proof_roadmap: Two presentations and factorisation of stages of the source (proof lines 4555-4562).
Fibre products with stages of the target, and the diagram (proof lines 4562-4568).
The dotted arrow by descent of an inclusion of ideals (proof lines 4574-4589).
Cofinal countable subsystem, and the converse direction (proof lines 4571-4576, 4591-4593).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective and flat, the lemma asserts that the source is countably indexed if and only if the target is (statement lines 4548-4553). One direction is a citation; the other is a real argument. Assuming the source countably indexed, one writes both spaces as filtered colimits, and for each stage of the source finds a stage of the target through which it factors; conversely, for each stage of the target, the fibre product with the source is an affine scheme and therefore factors through some stage of the source (proof lines 4555-4568). The author then displays the resulting diagram and observes that the proof is complete once the dotted arrow -- a factorisation of one stage of the target through a later one -- exists (proof lines 4568-4574). That existence is established by choosing a stage above the two in question, translating the two closed subschemes into ideals of its coordinate ring, and using the hypothesis: the relevant fibre product is faithfully flat over the stage of the target, so the containment of the two ideals after extending along the source morphism descends to a containment of the ideals themselves (proof lines 4574-4589). Since the stages selected form a cofinal countable subsystem, the target is countably indexed (proof lines 4571-4576). The claim is H2: the argument builds a cofinal countable subsystem of a presentation and the single nontrivial step -- descent of an inclusion of ideals along a faithfully flat morphism -- is displayed with its reason.
